data.body:
AC EVIDENCE, verified against merged main (Gerrit 2090).

AC1-AC6: pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_tests_trigger.py, 28 passed. That covers the declaration-only diff selecting tests through content_triggered_overlays and overlay_union on BOTH a raw diff and its compose_diff_context output; the parametrised replay over the five cited real diffs (SELECT for d9e0f0e733, 721cb7d6ac, 1c2bf6e57b; DO NOT SELECT for the comment-only 24917e843b and the annotation-only 83d91d488c) plus the anonymous-declaration case; the portability trio (Go func under internal/, TS export function under app/, Ruby class under lib/) against the docs-fence and config-only negatives; the test-file-only and union-not-replacement cases; guard (vii) asserted through prompts.get_prompt('code-review-tests'); and the overlay_union description naming the added-declaration trigger.

AC7 no regression, no baseline edit: the four named suites are green at 66 passed, and check_criteria_vocabulary.py exits 0. The 'unedited' half holds in its STRONG form - test_code_review_triggers.py and test_code_review_deletion_impact.py do not appear in the landed diff at all, so neither was edited rather than merely being edited compatibly.

Portability note, since this ticket is the one the epic's blocking project.portability criterion most directly applies to: the trigger is content-based, keyed on added declarations in the diff itself, and the acceptance criteria exercise Go, TypeScript and Ruby files outside src/ alongside Python. Nothing about the selection depends on GitHub Actions or any single CI provider.
